Case Studies / BBK Game Portal

BBK Game Portal
Case study · Consumer platform

A traditional Kuwaiti game, brought online for a new generation of players, in 30 days.

BBK is a web portal that lets people play a well-loved traditional Kuwaiti game online. Perennia delivered it turnkey for a team of young entrepreneurs, from the first requirement to a live, paying product.

Sector
Consumer entertainment
Engagement
Turnkey, requirements to launch
Time to launch
30 days
Platform
Full-stack JavaScript, payment gateways

The challenge

The game is part of everyday culture in Kuwait, but for most people it could only be played in person. A team of young entrepreneurs saw the opportunity to take it online. As a new venture, they had two firm constraints: the build had to cost as little as practically possible, and it had to be live quickly enough to test the idea in the market while it was still fresh.

The approach

The client came to us with an idea rather than a specification. We took ownership of the whole project — requirements, design, build, payments and launch — so the founders had one accountable partner instead of coordinating several contractors. Scope was held deliberately to what the business needed on day one, which is what made a 30-day launch achievable.

The solution: one turnkey delivery

  1. Requirements
  2. Design
  3. Build
  4. Payments
  5. Launch
  • A single full-stack JavaScript codebase — one language from browser to server, keeping the product simple and economical to run and extend.
  • Integrated payment gateways — players pay inside the portal, so the business could earn revenue from launch.
  • A straightforward player experience — a clean layout that gets players from the home page into a game in a few clicks.

The outcome

The portal launched within the planned 30 days and is live at playbbk.com.

  • Speed to market — the founders were testing their idea with real players within a month.
  • Controlled cost — a focused scope and a lean technology stack kept the investment proportionate to an early-stage venture.
  • Revenue-ready from day one — payments were part of the first release, not a later phase.
  • One accountable partner — a single team owned the outcome from requirements to launch.

What it demonstrates

  • Turnkey delivery for founders who have an idea but no technical team
  • Disciplined scoping to meet a fixed launch date and budget
  • Payments and commercial readiness built into the first release
